q: I self-host LangSmith on Kubernetes. How do I get its logs into my monitoring stack?
expected: all LangSmith services write logs to their node's filesystem and stdout; configure a collector (e.g. OpenTelemetry File Log Receiver, FluentBit tail input, Datadog Kubernetes log collection) to read them
evidence: write logs to their node's filesystem and to stdout
Ensure LangSmith services emit logs to stdout/stderr and forward them via [Fluent Bit](https://fluentbit.io/) or the Azure Monitor agent.

All services that are part of the LangSmith self-hosted deployment write logs to their node's filesystem and to stdout. In order to access these logs, you need to set up your collector to read from either the filesystem or stdout.

evidence: export trace data from a specific project and date range to an S3-compatible bucket

q: How do I remove PII from my traces before they reach LangSmith?
expected: Use the LangSmith SDK anonymizer (create_anonymizer with regex rules, or a third-party anonymizer like Presidio) passed to the Client, so data is masked before it is sent. An OpenTelemetry collector that redacts span attributes is also documented. Describing EITHER method correctly is enough.
evidence: runs a transform processor that redacts sensitive span attributes
LangSmith's [client libraries](/langsmith/mask-inputs-outputs) can remove sensitive content from traces before they are sent to LangSmith.

LangSmith provides multiple approaches to protect your data before it's sent to the backend:
- [Completely hide inputs and outputs](#hide-inputs-and-outputs)

You can create [anonymizers](/langsmith/mask-inputs-outputs#rule-based-masking-of-inputs-and-outputs) and apply them to
your graph using configuration.
